hints: Look carefully at the Km values for substrates 1 to 4 and notice they range from $4 \times 10^{-3}$ down to $1 \times 10^{-4}$ $mol\ dm^{-3}$, so ask yourself which end is smallest.

Recall what Km means for the Michaelis-Menten curve, the substrate concentration needed for half Vmax, and think whether a tightly binding substrate needs a lot or only a little to fill the active sites.
walkthrough:
**Remember what Km and affinity mean**

Think of affinity as how strongly the enzyme grabs the substrate. A high affinity means it holds on easily, even when very little substrate is around.

Key rule to remember:
$$low\ K_m = high\ affinity$$

**Compare the four Km values**

Let's list them in the same power of ten to see clearly:
$$A: 40 \times 10^{-4}, B: 10 \times 10^{-4}, C: 2 \times 10^{-4}, D: 1 \times 10^{-4}\ mol\ dm^{-3}$$
Substrate 4 clearly needs the lowest concentration to reach half Vmax.

**Choose the highest affinity**

Because substrate 4 has the smallest Km, the enzyme reaches half Vmax with the least substrate. That means the tightest binding and highest affinity, so answer D is correct.

options.A: Incorrect, $4 \times 10^{-3}$ is the largest Km, so it shows the lowest affinity, not the highest.
options.B: Incorrect, $1 \times 10^{-3}$ is smaller than A but still much larger than C and D, so affinity is only intermediate.
options.C: Incorrect, $2 \times 10^{-4}$ is low and shows good affinity, but it is still twice as large as D, so it is second best.
options.D: Correct, $1 \times 10^{-4}$ is the smallest Km, so the enzyme needs the least substrate to work well, showing the highest affinity.
